topic: Internal ballistics, grain configuration and form function
syllabus_extract: Internal ballistics, grain configuration and form function. D Resells energy equation and secondary energy losses, muzzle velocity and peak pressure analysis
specific_objectives: 37.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain about various branches of ballistics

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of PPT slides on grain configuration; Instructor supervision required for Q&A
intro_questions: What are the four main branches of ballistics?
Define internal ballistics in the context of gunnery.
List the primary factors affecting projectile motion inside the barrel.

development.content:
Branches of ballistics overview
Internal ballistics definition
Propellant energy equation
Secondary energy losses
Muzzle velocity analysis

Grain configuration types
Form function concept
Peak pressure analysis
Burn rate characteristics
Pressure curve interpretation

Energy loss mechanisms
Gas dynamics in barrel
Muzzle velocity calculation
Pressure peak determination
Efficiency of propellant

summary_questions: Explain how grain configuration influences the pressure curve.
Describe the relationship between form function and muzzle velocity.
Identify two sources of secondary energy losses in internal ballistics.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how changing the grain shape affects the peak pressure and muzzle velocity, referencing the next lesson on external ballistics.
